title: Both roots checked out — in the wrong equation
problem: An AI tutor solved \(\sqrt{x + 6} = x\) over the reals and checked both answers at the end. Tap the step that slips, or call it clean.
steps: Square both sides to clear the square root: \(x + 6 = x^2\).
Move all terms to one side: \(x^2 - x - 6 = 0\).
Check both values in \(x + 6 = x^2\): \(3 + 6 = 9 = 3^2\) and \(-2 + 6 = 4 = (-2)^2\), so both \(x = 3\) and \(x = -2\) are valid solutions.

clean_steps: Start from \(\sqrt{x + 6} = x\). Since the principal square root is non-negative, any real solution must satisfy \(x \ge 0\).
Square both sides to get \(x + 6 = x^2\).
Check in the original equation \(\sqrt{x + 6} = x\): \(\sqrt{9} = 3\) works, but \(\sqrt{4} = 2 \neq -2\), so \(x = -2\) is extraneous. Only \(x = 3\) solves the equation.

errors.original: Check both candidates in the original equation \(\sqrt{x + 6} = x\): \(\sqrt{9} = 3\) holds, while \(\sqrt{4} = 2 \neq -2\), so only \(x = 3\) is a solution.
errors.corrupted: Check both values in \(x + 6 = x^2\): \(3 + 6 = 9 = 3^2\) and \(-2 + 6 = 4 = (-2)^2\), so both \(x = 3\) and \(x = -2\) are valid solutions.
errors.why_wrong: Checking in the squared equation \(x + 6 = x^2\) can't catch extraneous roots created by squaring. In the original equation, \(\sqrt{-2 + 6} = 2 \neq -2\), so \(x = -2\) fails.
errors.why_tempting: Both substitutions look completely honest and accurate — it's easy to miss that they plugged into step 2 instead of step 1.
errors.catch_rule: After squaring both sides of an equation, always plug every candidate back into the original equation (before squaring).
errors.hint: Plug \(x = -2\) into the original equation \(\sqrt{x + 6} = x\), not the squared one.

meta.blurb: It actually substituted both roots at the end to verify — and still got fooled.
